Adaptive Multiresolution Extraction with Oracle is a technique that adaptively extracts meshes from coarser-resolution nodes to gain speed, using an 'oracle' structure to manage level of detail and patch cracks at resolution junctions [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that Westermann et al. gained speedups by 'adaptively deciding to extract the mesh from fewer, coarser-resolution nodes'. It identifies the main problem as 'cracks' appearing at junctions where finer-resolution cells are adjacent to coarser cells. It further explains that they built an 'oracle' structure in a single pass to determine the level of detail (depth) based on view-dependent and geometric criteria, and that they 'patch the resulting meshes to guarantee continuity' at these junctions. All specific details in the claim are present in the evidence.
